title: Contrix Cursor
description: Single opaque cursor type. Used as both stream continuation token (incremental sync, list pagination — 'since', 'after_cursor', 'prev_cursor', 'next_cursor') and barrier token (read-your-writes wait — 'X-Contrix-Wait-For'). The wire form is always cx:cursor:<base64url(canonical_json)>. Clients MUST treat the wire form as opaque; only the issuing server reads the inner structure. The 'purpose' field discriminates how the cursor is consumed.

purpose.description: Cursor purpose. 'stream' = continuation cursor for incremental sync (use as 'since' on /sync, 'after_cursor' on /federation/pull-operations, etc.). 'barrier' = read-your-writes / wait-for-event cursor (use in X-Contrix-Wait-For header to block until local frontier covers target.event_id). 'stream' cursors MAY include 's' (Space frontiers) and 'd' (device positions). 'barrier' cursors MUST include 'target'.

s.description: Per-Space frontier (stream cursors). Key is space_id; value pins the frontier this cursor describes for that Space.

target.description: Required when purpose='barrier'. Identifies the specific event whose causal frontier the consumer must reach before answering.

x.description: Expiration timestamp (Unix ms). MUST be in the future when the cursor is issued. TTL upper bounds (cursor lifetime = x - t_ms): barrier cursors MUST have TTL ≤ 3,600,000 ms (1 hour); stream cursors MUST have TTL ≤ 604,800,000 ms (7 days). Issuing a cursor exceeding these caps is a producer error; receivers MUST reject with `invalid_param`. Reasoning: barrier cursors only gate read-your-writes wait latency and become meaningless once the global frontier has long covered the target event. Stream cursors lose causal alignment value over weeks of activity.

^_[A-Za-z0-9_]*$.description: Server-private fields (compression flags, MACs, signatures). Names MUST start with underscore. Excluded from cursor migration translation; included in canonical bytes for the local server's MAC/integrity check.
